ONE CITY · ONE FULL STORY

What the hosts experience in one episode.

In each city, the hosts arrive as the audience’s guides into a complete Carnival Careers story: they meet the selected family and local workers, spend time with them at a major women’s sports game as part of the city experience, move through the arena with the cast while capturing the energy of the fans, merchandise, food, sponsors and game-day economy, then sit down together for the family dinner inside the arena restaurant, where the personal story, ambitions and challenges of the family become the emotional foundation of the episode. From there, the hosts follow the family through the housing journey—property selection, design decisions, construction or renovation, employment and ownership planning—while also participating in the city’s transit activation, City Hall and community moments, Carnival and cultural experiences, rehearsals and behind-the-scenes television production. The episode builds toward the completed home reveal and then the arena concert, where the same hosts who spent the week getting to know the family now bring that story in front of thousands of people, connecting the family, the city, the sports organization, artists, sponsors and audience into one continuous experience. By the time they leave the city, the hosts have not simply presented a concert or interviewed a family; they have lived through the city with them, attended its games, eaten together, watched a home and employment pathway take shape, participated in its culture, and carried the entire story from the first introduction to the final arena stage.

The story and the economic engine are the same thing

The Featured Woman

Every city begins with a living woman whose contribution deserves more light. She chooses a Carnival-culture family. They meet at dinner, and that relationship opens the whole city: her history, the family's reality, the home, the work, the businesses, the culture and the money moving around them. The arena concert is the victory lap — never the beginning — because by the time the city gathers, the story has already created something real.

Sideline Sitters

Childcare coordinated around the work. Tell us the shift, call time, rehearsal, event day, hotel stay or recurring schedule you need covered. We turn it into a complete care request, route it to an appropriate childcare partner, track the response and keep working the request until a provider confirms it or we have to tell you that no verified option is available.

Request coverage Provider capacity Employer / sponsor funding Check request status
THE SERVICE PROMISE

Childcare should not be the reason a parent misses the work.

Sideline Sitters is the coordination layer. We do not pretend to be the daycare, sitter agency or employer. Our job is to make a family request usable, route it against real provider capacity, keep the family informed and make sure a request does not quietly die after the first “no.”

Family intakeOne complete request
RoutingFit + capacity first
FallbackRe-route when possible
Booking ruleProvider confirms it
01

We capture the real need

Location, date, hours, children’s ages, one-time or recurring schedule, care setting and work/event context are collected up front so a provider can actually decide whether it fits.

02

We route by fit

Requests can be matched to licensed home-childcare, centre-based backup care, in-home or in-hotel care, qualified sitter agencies or another suitable partner, depending on location, age, hours and current capacity.

03

We track and re-route

If a provider cannot take the request, Sideline Sitters can move it to another available partner rather than treating one decline as the end of the family’s search.

04

The provider owns the care

The accepting provider controls eligibility, caregiver assignment, screening, licensing or other compliance, enrolment, payment, cancellation terms and care delivery. A request is not a booking until that provider confirms it.

HOW A REQUEST MOVES

From “I need care” to a real answer.

1 · ReceivedYou submit the complete schedule and family basics and receive a Sideline Sitters reference number.
2 · RoutingWe turn the request into a provider-ready packet and route it according to service area, ages, hours, setting and capacity.
3 · Provider reviewThe childcare provider decides whether it can accept the family and what enrolment, rate, minimum, funding or registration rules apply.
4 · HandoffThe family completes the provider’s own registration, payment and any required secure care information directly with the provider.
5 · Confirmed or re-routedOnly provider confirmation makes it booked. If the first fit has no capacity, we can continue routing to another suitable partner when one is available.

Short-notice, evening, weekend, overnight, hotel, event and recurring requests can be submitted. Availability is always provider- and capacity-dependent. Do not put medical records, banking information or other sensitive personal data into this public form; the accepting provider collects protected care information through its own process.

TRAVEL / PLANE POOL

Fly private without pretending we operate the aircraft.

Family Street is the referral and marketing layer. Villiers and licensed providers handle quoting, contracting, payment, operations and safety.

Request a charter quote ↗
NO-GAP PLANE POOL

Quote first. Fill the aircraft. Confirm only when the trip is fully funded.

The pool is built around real charter economics, not an invented bargain fare. A licensed provider returns the all-in trip quote first; the seat pool then tests whether the fully funded charter seat price works for the route.

01

Get the live quote

No made-up fare before the licensed charter provider returns the all-in trip cost.

02

Open the pool

Use aircraft sized for roughly 7–50 passengers. Every occupied seat is part of the funding math, including production or cast travel.

03

Test the value

Compare the fully funded charter seat price against live group or scheduled airfare. “Cheap” is tested, not claimed.

04

Confirm at gap C$0

No flight confirms until committed cash covers 100% of the trip economics. Sponsors can lower an already-funded fare later; they are not required to make the flight work.

7–50 passenger poolLive quote firstSponsor-independent100% funded before confirmation

SWEETEV RIDES / TORONTO PREMIUM MOBILITY

Get the right vehicle, the right approval and the right driver into one working lane.

SweetEV Rides is the coordination layer for a Toronto premium-fleet path: vehicle sourcing, lease / finance structure, commercial-use permission, insurance, driver matching, Uber Black / Black SUV readiness and private transportation demand. We do not call a car approved, financed, insured, booked or earning until the party responsible for that step confirms it.

I need a vehicle I am a driver / chauffeur I need premium transportation Dealer / lessor / insurer / fleet partner Check status
THE SERVICE PROMISE

Do not sell a car lead. Move the vehicle all the way to usable.

The page now follows the same close sequence the real Toronto conversations require: screen the vehicle, obtain an executable lease / finance path, prove commercial-use permission and insurability, line up a suitable driver before delivery where possible, complete platform and municipal requirements, then activate revenue channels. If one lender, vehicle or driver path fails, the request stays alive while another qualified option is worked.

VehicleVerified fit first
CapitalWritten structure
DriverNo-idle-car plan
ActivationOnly after approvals
01

Vehicle fit

Black premium vehicle, current model eligibility, appropriate seating/interior, clean/non-branded title and usable Ontario registration path are screened before money moves.

02

Lease / finance fit

We ask for the exact cash-to-close, payment, term, fees, mileage, security/PPSA, buyout/residual, receivable holder, document list and written commercial-use permission instead of sending a blind credit application.

03

Commercial-use + insurance fit

Livery/rideshare permission and the insurer/lessor requirements are treated as gates, not afterthoughts. A lender that will finance only personal use does not satisfy this lane.

04

Driver + demand fit

We can line up an eligible driver/chauffeur and test app, airport, corporate, event, production and private-booking demand so the first vehicle is not acquired with no operating plan.

HOW A VEHICLE MOVES

From “find me a car” to an active premium fleet vehicle.

1 · Request receivedWe capture the city, use case, seats, preferred models, budget / cash available, ownership path and timing.
2 · Vehicle screenedModel/year, title, Ontario road-use path, interior, seating and current Uber or chauffeur-service fit are checked before commitment.
3 · Written capital structureDealer, lessor, captive, private-credit or auction route returns the actual price, deposit, payment, fees, term, buyout and documents.
4 · Insurance / commercial-use reviewThe lessor/lender and insurer must allow the intended paid-passenger use. Required endorsements, limits and lessor wording are confirmed before close.
5 · Driver / operator matchedWhere possible, a driver is pre-arranged before delivery and confirms interest, availability and economics directly—without emailing private driver records around.
6 · Platform / local activationUber, vehicle inspection, registration, commercial licensing and any airport or municipal permissions are completed by the responsible parties.
7 · Active or reroutedIf the vehicle, financing, insurance or driver fails, the file can reroute to another qualified option. Only a fully approved vehicle is marked active.

Uber’s Toronto requirements and eligible-vehicle lists change. This site only pre-screens; the exact vehicle and driver must be accepted under the current platform, insurance and local rules at activation. No credit pull, purchase, bid, lease, guarantee or movement of funds is authorized by a public form submission.

CURRENT TORONTO OPERATING GATES

The page reflects what the live conversations have actually established.

Lessor lane active

Commercial livery is possible only by exception and underwriting.

The active in-house lessor has confirmed willingness in principle to review a livery lease, subject to insurance and credit. Used-vehicle age, lease term and mileage must fit its underwriting rather than forcing a high-mileage unit.

Insurance gate defined

Use the lessor’s actual insurance standard.

For the current lessor review, the stated preliminary standard is C$10M third-party liability, OPCF 6A, the lessor named as required, maximum C$1,000 deductible, A- or better carrier, with a binder/quote acceptable for preliminary review for up to 30 days.

Driver lane conditional

Match the driver to the final vehicle category.

A GTA chauffeur network is open to a direct driver introduction, but the vehicle category affects driver interest and earning fit. A black Suburban was specifically recommended for broader airport/corporate/chauffeur demand, while the QX60 remains under review.

Auction fallback usable

Ontario road-use paperwork must be verified before bidding.

One broker route has confirmed Ontario-registration paperwork and refundable buying-power deposit mechanics for Canadian-yard purchases. Lot-level tax, auction fees, title status and road-use eligibility still have to be recalculated before any bid.

Do not use this lane

Export/parts-only Canadian-resident route.

A separate auction intermediary confirmed that its Canada-located vehicles are export/parts-only for Canadian residents. That route does not satisfy a normal Ontario road-use vehicle requirement.

Portal integration pending

Customer flow cannot depend on the private SweetEV portal.

LaunchBay confirmed MCP/Zapier authorization must come from the SweetEV account owner. Until that owner enables a supported integration, this page creates its own request references and handoff packets instead of pretending the private portal is a customer checkout.

VEHICLE PRE-SCREEN

Kill obvious bad fits before the finance application.

This is not Uber approval. It is a quick gate so a rebuilt title, wrong colour/interior, missing seating, unverified model or prohibited commercial use does not get carried deeper into the process.

Current Uber Toronto vehicle requirements ↗Uber Black requirements ↗

No idle vehicle

ORIGINAL SWEETEV COMMERCIAL MODEL

Keep the original promise visible, but label the model correctly.

The original working arrangement combined an arranged-vehicle commission with an owner/fleet rental-revenue lane. Those figures are planning/commercial references, not guaranteed consumer financing terms or guaranteed earnings.

Arranged-car reference

Working structure: C$2,714 × 3 = C$8,142 upfront package per arranged vehicle. The production-company share reference is 35% before the existing VISTIQ payoff threshold and 20% after it, subject to the current SweetEV agreement controlling.

Rental-share reference

Working model: C$150 per booked day to the vehicle owner/fleet lane. At 20 booked days, that is C$3,000 gross in a month before vehicle payment, insurance, charging/fuel, maintenance, cleaning, licensing, downtime, taxes and other costs.

The original six-cars-per-year figure is a sales target, not a promise to a buyer, driver or investor. The actual deal must be rebuilt from the final vehicle, credit/lease approval, commercial insurance, driver arrangement and realized utilization.

Working-model calculator

Gross only. This calculator intentionally does not invent a lease payment, insurance premium, utilization rate or net profit.

INVESTORS

Back the company that takes the Carnival Careers model city to city.

We combine housing, work, operating businesses, Caribbean culture, live events, travel, commerce and filmed media. Investors can back the operating company or a specific asset deal — without pretending those are the same investment.

Start a private conversationRequest diligence
What you are buying into

One repeatable city engine.

A family story becomes housing and work. The city becomes the stage. The event creates attention. Media extends it. Commerce, sponsorship, travel and business activity turn that attention into revenue. Then the model moves to the next city.

Your lane

Choose the part you actually want to invest in.

01

Operating-company equity

The current company-level conversation is a C$3M seed round for the repeatable media, live-experience, commerce, distribution and operating system. Counsel has discussed a parent company with operating subsidiaries as one possible structure; final securities terms are not yet set.

For seed, media, culture, commerce and platform investors
02

Property and acquisition capital

Real estate is financed separately. Each property or portfolio is meant to stand on its own purchase price, appraisal, lender terms, equity requirement, release schedule and exit. The current Vic Towns conversation is active but still financing- and documentation-gated.

For real-estate equity, bridge and JV capital
03

Operating-business acquisitions

Grocery and other cash-flow businesses can sit beside the city platform as operating assets. Seller financing, institutional debt and purchaser capital are negotiated at the business level rather than hidden inside the entertainment budget.

For acquisition and cash-flow investors
04

City-by-city strategic capital

As the rollout travels, local capital can participate in a specific city, asset, operating business or launch rather than funding the entire 65-city vision at once.

For family offices, local partners and strategic co-investors

LENDERS

Finance the asset. See the repayment path. Keep the story separate.

Carnival Careers needs lenders who can underwrite real estate, business acquisitions and other defined facilities on normal credit logic. We bring the wider platform; the loan still has to make sense on collateral, cash flow, equity, controls and exit.

Send your credit boxSee diligence path
What you are lending into

Defined facilities, not one giant mixed ask.

Property debt should be paid by property economics. Business-acquisition debt should be paid by the business. Event and media revenue can strengthen the broader company, but it is not used as a substitute for sound underwriting.

Lending lanes

Where a lender can fit.

01

Senior real-estate financing

Acquisition or refinance facilities sized against the lower of acceptable LTV, LTC, DSCR/debt-yield and sale-release constraints. The current Toronto lender conversation is centered on a Vic Towns unit-block acquisition with the final property schedule and closing economics still being confirmed.

Banks, credit unions, mortgage funds and institutional lenders
02

Bridge and private mortgage capital

For deposits, timing gaps, renovations or acquisition closings where a short-duration facility can be secured, documented and taken out by sale, refinance or permanent debt.

Private lenders, MICs and bridge funds
03

CMHC / insured multifamily financing

Where a property qualifies, affordability, accessibility, energy performance, rent roll, building condition, borrower strength and reserves can be packaged for lender and CMHC review. No insured financing is called approved before it is approved.

CMHC-capable lenders and multifamily specialists
04

Business-acquisition debt

Operating businesses can use a mix of purchaser equity, institutional debt and seller VTB. Current acquisition work has included seller-financing structures where the seller carries a large portion of the price.

Commercial lenders and acquisition-finance specialists
Current file

What the lender needs to get to a real yes.

The current Vic Towns dialogue remains active. The broker side has asked for a stronger deposit and has encouraged a same-day closing of the unit block. We are not representing those requests as funded until the capital and credit package actually supports them.

Collateral and valuation

Final unit schedule, purchase contracts, appraisal instructions, title/status, legal review and asset-specific due diligence.

Credit structure

Maximum leverage, equity requirement, rate, fees, term, amortization, recourse, reserves, covenants and closing timeline.

Release and repayment

Unit-by-unit release prices where applicable, controlled funds flow and senior lender repayment before investor profit distributions.

Current lender relationships

We are already in the market.

CIBCA financing-screening conversation is scheduled for September 11. It is a screening discussion, not an approval.
Prime FinanceMalcolm Ramsay confirmed that his firm underwrites, structures and funds residential and commercial mortgages; the immediate request has been narrowed to property financing.
Seller-financed acquisitionsCurrent business-acquisition work includes vendors willing to discuss meaningful VTB structures, reducing the amount that must come from an institutional lender at closing.
TRC SolarTRC Solar has opened a property-energy discussion around solar/EV infrastructure without upfront capital or added debt, subject to site-specific review. That can reduce capex pressure; it is not presented as mortgage proceeds.

Lend with us city by city.

As Carnival Careers travels, we want a lender network that can handle local real estate, operating businesses, multifamily, bridge needs, fleet/equipment and other financeable assets without forcing every city into the same credit product.

Work with us

Do not send personal KYC, banking credentials or sensitive borrower information through this public form. Those belong in the lender's secure process.

Help us close the work in Toronto — then come with us around the world.

How we work

Own an outcome.

We want scope, fee, timing, dependencies and a named person responsible. The best service partner makes the next decision easier and leaves behind a process we can reuse.

One city or many

Take one Toronto mandate, a single transaction, or help build a standard that can follow the 65-city rollout.

One discipline or a coordinated team

Specialists are welcome. So are firms that can coordinate several related disciplines without blurring responsibility. Strong capital and sponsor relationships are a plus.

Paid work begins only when approved

A conversation, proposal or site submission does not authorize fees. Scope and authority must be clear before work starts.

Build the bench in every city.

Toronto is not the finish line. Current expansion planning has included North America, the Caribbean and Europe. We want local and international professionals who can become trusted regional partners as each new city is underwritten and activated.

ORDER OF EXECUTION

First control the assets. Then commit capital. Then produce and sell the show.

Day 0–30Control assets: agreements, appraisal, title and diligence.
Day 31–60Commit capital: senior debt, VTB, investor account and buyer-takeout paths.
Day 61–90Lock the show: venue, artists, production, TV, City Hall, transit, vendors and sponsors.
Month 4–12Produce + sell: film the episode, run the concert, collect sales and place households.
After contractsLaunch cruise only after charter, sponsor and passenger documents are in place.
